book: Ramayana, the Epic of Rama, Prince of India, condensed into English verse by Romesh C. Dutt (1899)

chunks.why: Rama bends Rudra's bow, wins Sita, weddings, joyous return to Ayodhya, Rama beloved.
Dasa-ratha decides to crown Rama, city rejoices; Manthara begins poisoning Kaikeyi.
City decorated for coronation, but Kaikeyi demands Bharat's crown and Rama's exile.
King's anguished lament; Rama arrives to find his father grief-stricken and speechless.
Kaikeyi tells Rama he must go to fourteen-year jungle exile; Sita insists on following.
Departure into exile, Ayodhya weeping; Rama, Sita, Lakshman cross Ganges to Bharad-vaja.
Settle peacefully at Chitra-kuta; dying father recalls old curse, weeps for banished son.
Dasa-ratha dies; Bharat comes to jungle, begs Rama to return; Rama refuses, honored by all.
Rama gives sandals to Bharat as regent, moves deeper into forest; welcomed at Atri's hermitage.
Agastya arms Rama; peaceful cottage life at Panchavati; mild winter with Sita and Lakshman.
Surpa-nakha mutilated; Ravan plots vengeance; golden deer lures Rama away, Sita left alone with hermit-Ravan.
Ravan abducts Sita, Jatayu dies fighting; anguished Rama seeks Sugriva's alliance in exile.
Rama slays Bali, crowns Sugriva; through the rains he waits, then Vanar armies dispatched to search.
Hanuman finds Sita alive in Lanka's Asoka grove, gives Rama's ring, brings back her jewel and news.
Rama pledges vengeance; in Ravan's council Bibhishan defects to Rama, strengthening his cause.
War opens; Indrajit's serpent-noose fells both Rama and Lakshman senseless on the battlefield.
Revived, Rama slays Kumbha-karna; brothers again felled by Indrajit's magic, then Lakshman kills him.
Ravan wounds Lakshman with Sakti; Indra sends celestial chariot; Rama slays Ravan, funerals held.
Fire vindicates Sita; aerial-car return to Ayodhya; brothers reunited; Rama consecrated, golden reign.
Horse-sacrifice; sons recognized; recalled Sita, shamed by rumor, is swallowed by Earth; Rama's bliss ends and he dies.
